●Depth efficiency

Deep Neural Network - Summary
●Deep feed-forward Neural Networks:
data propagated through the network to predict the output
●Deep architectures:
●are more efficient than shallow and more powerful (model non-linearity more
easily)
●are a good model for hierarchical data (images and language among others).
●work well in practice
●are still difficult to design and train, not always fully understood
●usually require a lot of infrastructure
●…

Optimisation —> best way to find the parameters.
We know how to measure how good a set of parameters is.
Start with random weights. Iteratively refine to get lower loss.
Some options …
•Random search or “local” search: not ideal for DL. Used in other problems
•Follow the “gradient”: vector of derivatives for each dimension of input space
○compute gradient of loss function with respect to model weights W
○step size (learning rate)
hyperparameter
source: http://cs231n.github.io

=== PDF PAGE 32 ===
●Optimisation - Gradient Descent (GD) & Deep Learning.
○Ideally, find the exact minimum. Actually, not feasible. N is very large (#samples). W
has too many params (1K-1000K)

○Saddle points are a problem. Many methods get stuck there.
Stochastic GD has better chances.



○Stochastic GD (SGD): start “improving” from the first sample processed. One
step per sample (or per mini-batch: 32, 64, 128, 256, … No more that you can fit
in your CPU/GPU memory!).
○Most common training strategy in DL: SGD + Backpropagation (later)
GD: for all samples  (or Batch GD)
SGD: for one sample (or a few)

=== PDF PAGE 35 ===
Properties of SGD
●Can escape from local minima
●Adds noise, but still sensible updates as based on part of data
●Uses all data equally
●Less computationally expensive
●Seems to find better solutions
●Doesn’t converge in traditional sense
●Learning rate schedule – decrease learning rate over time

=== PDF PAGE 36 ===
●Optimisation - SGD - Still many challenges for the vainilla version
¿
✅
❌ ? BGDSGD
1. redundant computations for similar examples
2. faster
3. high variance and high fluctuations during training
4. converges to the minimum of the “basin” where it starts
5. needs to shuffle training data
6. suitable for online or incremental learning
What’s true for which variation?
Fundamentals of DL - Optimisation

=== PDF PAGE 37 ===
●Optimisation - SGD -
Many optimization algorithms with different
properties
○Loss surface contours and time evolution of
different algorithms (behaviours, speeds, stuck-
points, …)
○Adaptive learning-rate - LR per param, adapted
at each step) - best compromise in saddle point
problems (where  Vainilla SGD gets stuck).
○Weight-decay - reduce weight values at each
step. Can be equivalent to L2 regularization term.
In adaptive approaches use “decoupled” version
(as in AdamW)
Images credit: Alec Radford.
Fundamentals of DL - Optimisation
